title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 434
paragraphs: He did many such acts of madness both to Persians and to allies, remaining at Memphis and opening ancient tombs and examining the dead bodies. Likewise he entered the temple of Hephaistos and mocked the image of the god at length; for the image of Hephaistos closely resembles the Phoenician Pataicoi that the Phoenicians carry about on the prows of their triremes — for anyone who has not seen these, I will describe their appearance: it is the likeness of a dwarfish man. He entered also into the temple of the Cabeiroi, into which no one is permitted to enter except the priest alone, and the images there he even set on fire, after first mocking them a great deal. These too are like the images of Hephaistos, and it is said they are the children of that god.
